Chest x‑ray shows a diffuse ground‑glass pattern with air bronchograms — the radiographic hallmark of surfactant deficiency. Maternal gestational diabetes is an additional risk factor because fetal hyperinsulinemia can delay surfactant production. Other causes (transient tachypnea of the newborn, pneumonia, meconium aspiration) are less consistent with the combination of prematurity, radiographic ground‑glass pattern with air bronchograms, and progressive respiratory compromise. Therefore the most likely diagnosis is surfactant deficiency–related neonatal respiratory distress (hyaline membrane disease).

DIAGNOSIS: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (surfactant deficiency / hyaline membrane disease)
